results.title: African journalists adopt a continental action plan on responsible AI, decent work and media freedom
results.content: African journalist leaders have adopted an advocacy action plan to advance responsible artificial intelligence (AI), decent working conditions and quality journalism across the continent. The plan was agreed at the close of a two-day dialogue and capacity-building programme convened by the Federation of African Journalists (FAJ) in Addis Ababa on 24-25 October 2026.

results.content: The Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC) is predicting petrol prices to go down while diesel price go up at the pumps in the first pricing window starting, November 1, 2026. results.title: PMI, TIME Studios spotlight projects delivering climate solutions at scale
results.content: TIME Studios and the Project Management Institute (PMI), the world’s leading authority for project professionals, have announced Season 2 of The Solutionaries, a documentary series about the project success behind climate solutions that scale and what it takes to move from a solution that works once to one that works everywhere.

results.title: Level Up Conference empowers 360 young people in Ashanti Region
results.content: The 2026 Level Up Conference has empowered 360 young people in the Ashanti Region, equipping them with essential knowledge, skills, and practical strategies to advance their careers, entrepreneurial pursuits, and personal growth in a competitive job market.

results.title: Prof Bokpin calls for a national review of Mahama’s fight against galamsey
results.content: Professor of Finance and Economist at the University of Ghana, Prof Godfred Bokpin, has called for a national review of the Mahama administration’s fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, saying the government’s interventions appear inadequate compared with the scale of destruction caused by the practice.

results.title: NACOC destroys cannabis farms in Nadowli District
results.content: The Upper West Regional Command of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), in a joint operation with officers of the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS), has destroyed several cannabis farms at Siiru, a community in the Nadowli District of the Upper West Region.

results.title: NAIMOS not adequately equipped to fight galamsey – Awula Serwah
results.content: The Executive Director of EcoConscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has raised concerns about the operational capacity of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), questioning whether it has the necessary equipment and logistical support to effectively combat illegal mining.

results.title: Galamsey fight remains ineffective despite NAIMOS arrests and seizures – Awula Serwah
results.content: The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, says Ghana has yet to make meaningful progress in the fight against illegal mining, warning that the country remains at risk of an ecological catastrophe.

results.title: Galamsey: Ghana still faces national emergency, says Awula Serwah
results.content: The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has warned that Ghana remains in a national emergency over illegal mining, insisting that current interventions have not delivered the environmental progress needed to protect the country's natural resources.

results.title: Gov’t wants to use Traffitech-GH to extort money from drivers while traders take over spaces – GPRTU
results.content: Commercial transport operators have accused the government of seeking to use the planned rollout of the Traffitech-GH system to extort money from drivers through traffic fines while allowing traders to occupy designated bus stops and pedestrian walkways.

results.title: Transport operators threaten nationwide strike as Traffitech-GH begins on Nov 1
results.content: Commercial transport operators have threatened to suspend services nationwide on November 1, when the Traffitech-GH system is scheduled to become operational, accusing the government and the police of failing to clear traders from designated bus stops and pedestrian walkways.

results.title: Akim Swedru MP supports 145 traders, apprentices and artisans
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has provided financial and skills development support to 145 constituents as part of efforts to promote entrepreneurship and vocational training.

results.title: ‘We cannot feed our families’ — 170 college staff withdraw services
results.content: About 170 staff of the Savannah College of Education at Daboya in the Savannah Region have withdrawn their services over delays in migrating them onto the government payroll, more than a year after the institution was absorbed into the public Colleges of Education system.

results.title: NDC cannot preach accountability and resist scrutiny — Afenyo-Markin
results.content: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of adopting double standards on accountability, insisting that the party must accept the same scrutiny it demanded of the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration.

results.title: NDC must accept the same scrutiny demanded under Akufo-Addo—Afenyo-Markin
results.content: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has challenged the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) to uphold the accountability standards it championed during its eight years in opposition, insisting that a change of government must not shield public officials from scrutiny.

results.title: Bekwai MP commissions new mechanised borehole for Zongo community
results.content: The Member of Parliament (MP) for Bekwai, Ralph Poku-Adusei, has commissioned and handed over a newly constructed mechanised borehole to the Bekwai Zongo community as part of efforts to improve access to clean and reliable drinking water in the constituency.

results.title: Businessman granted GH¢400k bail in alleged US$3.5m fraud case
results.content: An Adenta Circuit Court has granted bail to a businessman allegedly involved in a US$3.5 million fraud case.

results.title: GPA bemoans weak national book policy and enforcement of copyright laws, marks 50th anniversary with national symposium
results.content: The Ghana Publishers Association (GPA) has observed the lack of a comprehensive national book policy and weak enforcement of copyright laws continue to hamper the growth of the Ghanaian publishing industry.

results.title: The cost of staying alive: diabetes, hypertension and the price of a working life in Ghana
results.content: The World Health Organisation (WHO) reported that the number of people living with diabetes worldwide rose from 200 million in 1990 to 830 million in 2022. In 2022, approximately 14 per cent of adults aged 18 and older had diabetes.

results.title: Shoe-making is not for school dropouts — Horseman founder Tonyi Senayah
results.content: Founder of Horseman, Tonyi Senayah, says his shoemaking business is driven by a broader mission to create fulfilling employment opportunities for artisans and challenge the perception that vocational trades are meant for people who fail to progress through formal education.

results.title: MTN Ghana reports 44.4% growth in mobile money transactions as digital services expand
results.content: MTN Ghana has reported a 44.4 per cent year-on-year increase in the value of Mobile Money transactions for the first half of 2026, alongside plans to invest US$1.1 billion over three years to expand its network infrastructure and digital services across the country.

results.title: Police arrest woman, offer GH¢100,000 reward for Sakumono murder suspect
results.content: The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 47-year-old woman in connection with the killing of two relatives at the NTHC Estate, Sakumono, in the Greater Accra Region, and declared the principal suspect wanted.

results.title: This Saturday on Prime Insight: NPP restructuring, galamsey fight and presidential tenure
results.content: Political party restructuring, the fight against illegal mining and the legal challenge over presidential tenure are expected to dominate discussions on Joy Prime’s Prime Insight programme on Saturday, October 31.

results.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
results.content: The US has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically-needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks, after Kyiv said deliveries had been delayed in recent months.

results.title: Ghana and Burkina Faso seek stronger trade and industrial cooperation at SIAO 2026
results.content: Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening trade and investment relations with Burkina Faso through a proposed bilateral trade agreement aimed at promoting industrial cooperation, cross-border trade and value addition.
